justification: Uses asbestos-exposed MexTAg CC mouse tumors to build a prognostic survival gene signature; does not study genetic effect on susceptibility.
CC-MexTAg cross exposed to asbestos; host genetics affect MM latency/survival with QTL and modifier genes identified for susceptibility.
Germline Bap1-mutant mice given asbestos show higher MM incidence and earlier onset versus wild-type; clear genetic susceptibility study.

Genetic mesothelioma mouse model plus amosite asbestos; asbestos accelerates MM onset and tumour burden.
Chemoprevention drug study in a fixed genetic model; genotype's effect on susceptibility is not the variable studied.
ADAR2 RNA-editing study focused on chemoresistance and tumor microenvironment, not on genetic effect on mesothelioma susceptibility.
RBM8A RNA-editing translational-regulation mechanism, mainly cell-based; no engineered genetic modification affecting in-vivo mesothelioma susceptibility.
Biochemical BAP1-HMGB1-HDAC1 gene-environment mechanism; no mouse mesothelioma incidence, latency, or burden measured.
Translatome and mTOR-inhibitor therapy study; genetic loss is background, not a studied determinant of susceptibility.
Blm+/- mice exposed to asbestos show shorter survival and higher mesothelioma incidence; germline mutation increases susceptibility.
Conditional HMGB1-knockout mice, asbestos; measures mesothelial transformation/foci rather than tumor incidence, but genetic modification and susceptibility mechanism integral.
Mth1/Mutyh/Ogg1 knockout mice given crocidolite; mesothelioma incidence and survival compared across genotypes.
Tests zeolite intervention in a transgenic mesothelioma model; fixed genotype, gene's effect on susceptibility not studied.
No abstract; on-topic title links carbon-nanotube-induced mesothelioma to gene loss; fibre-type and content ambiguous, cannot confidently exclude.
p53 mice exposed to MWCNTs developed no lung/pleural tumors; focus is pulmonary granuloma and immune response, not mesothelioma.
DMT1-transgenic mice given crocidolite; mesothelioma incidence and survival compared to wild-type, showing delayed carcinogenesis.
Asbestos-exposed NF2+/- and NF2+/-CR-/- mice; mesothelioma and survival assessed across genotypes.

Heterozygous germline Bap1-mutant mice; asbestos exposure significantly increases aggressive mesothelioma incidence versus wild-type.
